new_scholarship.name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (EMJM)
new_scholarship.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are high-level, fully integrated master's programmes designed and delivered jointly by at least three higher education institutions in at least three different countries, and they award either a joint degree or multiple degrees. The European Commission funds both the programmes and competitive scholarships for the best students worldwide. Applicants apply directly to the institution running their chosen programme, and each master's own website sets its own entry requirements and deadlines. Individual scholarships are worth EUR 1,400 per month for a maximum of 24 months.

new_scholarship.name: DAAD Scholarships (Deutscher Akademischer Austauschdienst Scholarship Database)
new_scholarship.description: DAAD administers a family of scholarship programmes for international students and researchers funded largely by the German Federal Foreign Office, listed in its official Scholarship Database at www2.daad.de. The flagship Study Scholarship for postgraduate study states scholarship payments of 992 euros a month, payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance, a travel allowance, and an annual study allowance of EUR 460. Funding is awarded for the standard period of study of the chosen programme, up to a maximum of 24 months, and must begin in 2027. Each individual programme in the database sets its own eligibility, deadline and award value, and application deadlines are updated annually in the second quarter.

new_scholarship.name: Japanese Government (MEXT / Monbukagakusho) Scholarship
new_scholarship.official_source: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), Japan
new_scholarship.description: The Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho) Scholarship is offered in seven types: Research students, Teacher training students, Undergraduate students, Japanese studies students, College of technology students, Specialized training college students, and the Young Leaders Program. Applicants apply either through embassy recommendation or, for most types, university recommendation. The published benefits are a monthly scholarship, tuition exemption, and round-trip travel expenses (airfare). Each type has its own age limit, academic qualification, field of study and duration, and MEXT directs applicants to the latest edition of the application guidelines because detailed requirements are established separately.
new_scholarship.duration: Varies by type: research students up to 2 years for the irregular course or the standard school year for the regular course; teacher training within 1 year and 6 months including Japanese language education; undergraduate students 5 years including Japanese language training (7 years for medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and veterinary science); Japanese studies students 4 years including Japanese language training (4 years and 6 months for merchant marine studies); college of technology students 3 years including Japanese language training; specialized training college students 1 year. Under university recommendation the duration depends on each school's quota, up to a standard school year
new_scholarship.deadline: With regard to application qualifications and procedures, in addition to the actual contents, there are also cases when detailed requirements are established. Because of this, be sure to confirm the latest edition of the application guidelines. If the application qualifications differ from the application guidelines, the contents of the guidelines should be followed.
new_scholarship.application_period: Embassy recommendation and university recommendation cycles are set per scholarship type and published in the MEXT application guidelines; the official page publishes no single central date
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Each type has its own eligibility. Research students must be under 35 and eligible for admission to a master's or doctoral programme at a Japanese graduate school. Teacher training students must be under 35, be graduates of a college or teacher training college, and have at least five years of active teaching experience in a primary, secondary or teacher training college in their home country. Undergraduate students must be under 25 and have completed 12 years of schooling or comparable study. Japanese studies students must be between 18 and 29 and be enrolled in a Japanese-language or Japanese-culture faculty at a university outside Japan. College of technology students must be under 25 with 11 or more years of education. Specialized training college students must be under 25 with 12 years of schooling.

application_readiness_checklist: Identify which of the seven scholarship types fits your age, prior education and field of study, because each has its own limits
Work out whether embassy recommendation or university recommendation is available for that type, since the Young Leaders Program takes neither
Download the latest edition of the MEXT application guidelines for your type, because they override the summary page

Plan for Japanese language training as part of the scholarship, which for several types comes before the degree programme

Applying to the Young Leaders Program directly, since nominations come only from official overseas recommending organisations
Missing that Japanese studies students must remain enrolled at their home institution when they return

alerts.message: MEXT states that detailed requirements are established separately and that if the application qualifications differ from the application guidelines, the contents of the guidelines should be followed. Always work from the latest guidelines.
The official page publishes no dates. Deadlines come from the embassy or consulate for embassy-recommended applicants and from the host university for university-recommended applicants.
The monthly scholarship is JPY 143,000-145,000 for research students, JPY 117,000 for teacher training students and JPY 242,000 for undergraduate students. Do not assume one rate for all types.
MEXT notes that the institutions offering preliminary training of Japanese may change, so do not rely on a specific preparatory school.

submission_workflow: Choose your scholarship type and confirm the application route available for it
Obtain the latest MEXT application guidelines for that type
Assemble the documents listed in the guidelines and, for embassy recommendation, your embassy or consulate's own forms
If taking the Applicant Qualifying Examinations - Subject Test, register and sit it in time
Submit through the embassy or consulate, or directly to the university for university recommendation
Wait for selection and, on award, complete Japanese language training where the scholarship includes it
